Elena — thanks for sending these over and for the call. Received the attachments (W-9 + bank letter).

Quick checklist from our side so we have the correct handoffs:
- I'll kick off vendor enrollment with Procurement and ask them to queue a payment validation (micro-deposits) with Finance.
- Please confirm the exact remittance reference format you want on the wire/ACH (you listed CRSTLN_INV# — is that final?).
- Confirm the invoice email address where remittance advices should be sent (we have finance@crestlinelabs.com on file).

Also: can you confirm the legal entity EIN as shown on the W-9 (we need that to match our supplier record)? If you'd rather not paste here, a quick reply with the 9-digit EIN will do.

When micro-deposits post we'll need you to reply with the two deposit amounts (we'll instruct Finance to use a two-deposit test). Expect that process to take 24–72 hours depending on bank clearing. Once validated, Procurement will create the Redwood PO and tag your vendor record so invoices auto-match.

If all good I'll hand this off to Marissa (cc'd) to create the PO and to Laura for the payment test.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Elena — welcome, and thanks for providing the documents.

I will create the Redwood PO once Finance confirms the two micro-deposit values. Two quick notes from Procurement:
- Please include the preferred remittance descriptor on your invoice as a separate field (invoice header or remittance line) so our AP automation can parse it reliably.
- If your invoices include multiple sub-accounts, add the internal account code in the invoice notes so we can map the PO properly.

Action items on our side:
- Marissa (Procurement) will request a micro-deposit verification job from Finance (Laura).
- Once Finance confirms the deposits and Elena replies with the amounts, I'll generate PO RED-2028-0919-CL and send it to the vendor contact on file.

Laura — can you schedule the ACH test today and confirm the amounts back to this thread? If possible, please use the descriptor "CRSTLN_TST" for the test so it's easy to spot.

Thanks — Marissa
